description: Primary care clinicians must be highly skilled in preventive medicine, cardiovascular risk factors, day-to-day clinical problems, chronic disease management, communication skills, and optimal use of diagnostic tests and new medications. Health disparities and the care of vulnerable patients are a central part of our daily practice as we try to maximize quality, safety, equity, and value. Close collaboration with other specialists, inpatient colleagues, and diverse teams of health professionals is essential for the care of our complex patients. In addition to a full discussion of common problems in primary care and preventive medicine, this course will also focus on clinical skills and problem-solving in dermatology, women’s health, clinical nutrition, neurology, psychiatry, infectious diseases, and interprofessional collaboration. The course will utilize formal lectures, case discussions, practical workshops, an audience response system, questions and answers, and a detailed syllabus. Participate in person at the Everline Resort in Lake Tahoe or tune in virtually for this 6 day conference. Included in your registration fee is access to the course recordings on demand after the conference and for 30 days after the course.
locationName: Everline Resort & Spa, a Hyatt Hotel

description: Indoor Air Quality – Mold in the Home Presented by: Timur Durani, MD Occupational and Environmental Medicine Specialist UCSF Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland Planners expect learners to: 1. Differentiate evidence-based health effects associated with indoor mold exposure from unvalidated claims regarding “toxic mold” and mycotoxin-related illness. 2. Evaluate patients with suspected mold exposure using an appropriate clinical approach, including recognition of allergies, hypersensitivity, and rare infectious manifestations. 3. Identify environmental, socioeconomic, housing-quality, and cultural factors that influence mold exposure risk and apply strategies to reduce implicit bias when evaluating patients with environmental health concerns. description: What’s next in genomics workflows? Join us for a Lunch & Learn exploring the technologies and strategies that enable high-quality next-generation sequencing (NGS) data generation, improved reproducibility, and greater efficiency in genomics research. The session will highlight genomics workflows from sample preparation through NGS, including automation with Bravo systems, quality control using Fragment Analyzer and TapeStation systems, and SureSelect target enrichment solutions. Attendees will learn how these technologies work together to streamline workflows, improve data quality, and support a wide range of applications from basic research to translational genomics studies. The Agilent team will share insights into the latest tools and approaches for optimizing genomics workflows and enabling more reproducible sequencing results. The session will conclude with an open discussion about your research goals, current workflows, and the challenges you are facing in generating reliable sequencing data. Enjoy a complimentary lunch while connecting with colleagues and learning about the latest advances in genomics technologies. Seats are limited. Reserve your spot today: https://humangenetics.ucsf.edu/lunch-and-learn-tech-seminar-series-agilent We encourage you to share this invitation with colleagues and collaborators who may be interested. We look forward to seeing you!
